source_title: Neuronal types in the mouse amygdala and their transcriptional response to fear conditioning
node_relevance_reason: Directly describes scRNA-seq taxonomy of 130 mouse amygdala neuronal cell types including GABAergic and glutamatergic types, relevant to basal_amygdala_fear_neuron, bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell, bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron, cea_large_aspiny_neuron, cea_small_aspiny_neuron.
summary: This study presents a detailed cell-type taxonomy of the adult mouse amygdala using single-cell RNA sequencing on naive and fear-conditioned mice, identifying 130 neuronal cell types and validating their spatial distributions. A subset of all neuronal types is transcriptionally responsive to fear learning and memory retrieval. The atlas provides molecular identities for amygdala neurons across BLA, IA, and CEA compartments.
quotes: We perform single-cell RNA sequencing on naïve and fear-conditioned mice, identify 130 neuronal cell types and validate their spatial distributions.
A subset of all neuronal types is transcriptionally responsive to fear learning and memory retrieval.
The activated engram cells upregulate activity-response genes and coordinate the expression of genes associated with neurite outgrowth, synaptic signaling, plasticity and development.

source_title: Neuronal types in the mouse amygdala and their transcriptional response to fear conditioning
node_relevance_reason: Describes the three main neuronal classes (GABAergic 56 types, VGLUT1 32 types, VGLUT2 42 types) organized by transcription factor expression, directly relevant to molecular classification of basal amygdala fear/extinction neurons and BLA interneurons.
summary: The amygdala neuronal cell-type taxonomy resolves 56 GABAergic (Gad1/Gad2/Slc32a1), 32 VGLUT1 (Slc17a7), and 42 VGLUT2 (Slc17a6) cell types, each organized into branches sharing hierarchical combinatorial expression of homeodomain transcription factors. Neurons are robustly segregated by neurotransmitter identity, and the amygdala is described as a collection of nuclei belonging to striatal, cortical, and subplate structural-developmental regions.
quotes: 56 GABAergic cell types (Gad1, Gad2 and Slc32a1, 13,006 cells), 32 VGLUT1 types (Slc17a7, 11,947 cells) and 42 VGLUT2 types (Slc17a6, 5,232 cells).
Each neuron class was organized into branches of related cell types that shared hierarchical and combinatorial expression of (homeodomain) transcription factors.
The amygdala is a collection of anatomically and functionally defined nuclei belonging to the following three main structural-developmental regions: striatal, cortical and subplate amygdala nuclei.

source_title: Neuronal types in the mouse amygdala and their transcriptional response to fear conditioning
node_relevance_reason: Describes engram cell biology and amygdala subregion structure (BLA, IA, CEA) relevant to fear/extinction neurons; notes distinct cytoarchitecture and cell-type diversity across nuclei.
summary: The paper contextualizes amygdala engram cells and structural diversity: BLA, IA, and CEA cluster participate in emotional fear learning, and subregions have distinct cytoarchitecture, connectivity, and cell-type composition. Single-cell transcriptomics has previously characterized basolateral, central, and medial amygdala subtypes.
quotes: Emotional responses associated with fear learning involve basolateral amygdala (BLA), intercalated amygdala (IA) and central amygdala (CEA) clusters.
These subregions are defined by their distinct cytoarchitecture, connectivity and functionality, and have increasingly revealed great diversity in cell-type composition.

source_title: Neuronal types in the mouse amygdala and their transcriptional response to fear conditioning
node_relevance_reason: Discusses functional role of alternate molecular populations in amygdala circuits, the specificity of memories encoded by specific molecular cell types, and the importance of linking molecular description to functional roles — directly relevant to basal_amygdala_fear_neuron and basal_amygdala_extinction_neuron.
summary: The paper highlights that alternate emotional functions are often achieved through neuronal populations in the same regional circuitries, distinguished by different molecular identities. It emphasizes that the specificity of memories may be encoded by specific molecular cell types, motivating the systematic link between molecular cell-type descriptions and functional roles in the amygdala.
quotes: These alternate functions were often achieved through neuronal populations in the same regional circuitries, distinguished only by different molecular identities.

Given that the specificity of memories may be encoded by specific molecular cell types, linking the molecular description of amygdala cell types to their functional roles on a more systematic scale is of increasing Resource

source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Core evidence for bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell: directly describes NPY+ neurogliaform cell identification in BLA using Npy-Cre/Dlx5-6-Flp double-transgenic strategy, confirming NPY as a neurogliaform marker and performing electrophysiology on these cells.
summary: Using INTRSECT viral strategy in Npy-Cre;Dlx5/6-Flp mice to label only GABAergic NPY+ neurons, whole-cell recordings in EYFP-expressing neurons were performed in LA and BA acute slices. NPY is confirmed as a characteristic marker for neurogliaform cells. Three main GABAergic cell groups were identified among NPY+ neurons based on single-cell electrophysiological features including action potential half-width, maximum spiking rate, accommodation ratio, membrane time constant, and sag amplitude.
quotes: As NPY has been shown to be a characteristic marker for the vast majority, if not for all neurogliaform cells in cortical regions, we used Npy-Cre mice to label these GABAergic neurons in the amygdala.
To reveal the cell types that express NPY in the LA and BA, we performed whole-cell recordings in EYFP-expressing neurons in acute amygdalar

source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Provides electrophysiological classification of NPY+ interneurons into three groups in amygdala: neurogliaform (largest group with characteristic morphology, nNOS+, PV-, CB-), fast-spiking (PV+, CB+), and a third group. Directly defines bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell electrophysiology and marker profile.
summary: Three GABAergic cell groups among NPY+ amygdalar neurons were resolved: the largest group showed characteristic neurogliaform morphology (short smooth dendrites, dense local axonal arborization) with weak nNOS immunoreactivity (22/25) and no PV (0/9) or CB (0/25) or SST (0/4). A second group (33%) showed fast-spiking phenotype with narrow spikes, no accommodation, and PV+ (5/7) and CB+ (3/6) immunoreactivity.
quotes: Labeled interneurons in this group displayed characteristic morphological features of neurogliaform cells, including short smooth dendrites that often ramified and dense local axonal arborization.
Many of these interneurons showed weak immunoreactivity for nNOS (22/25 tested), but none for PV (0/9 tested), CB (0/25 tested) or SST (0/4 tested).
These interneurons had narrow spikes, the highest firing rate, no accommodation in spiking, fast membrane time constant and no sag.

source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Provides quantitative data on the fraction of NPY+ GABAergic neurons that are neurogliaform cells (PV-/SST-/CB-) in LA and BA amygdala, directly supporting bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell.
summary: About 25% of NPY+ GABAergic neurons in LA and BA expressed PV, and ~27% expressed SST. Triple immunostaining (PV/SST/CB negative) estimated neurogliaform cells at approximately 45% of NPY+ GABAergic neurons in Npy-Cre;Dlx5/6-Flp mice.
quotes: about half of the NPY+ GABAergic neurons (~ 45% in both amygdalar nuclei) was immunoreactive neither for PV nor for SST, a group of neurons that should correspond to neurogliaform cells.
neurogliaform cells may represent appr. 45 % of NPY+ GABAergic cells expressing EYFP but lacking immunoreactivity for PV, SST and CB

source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Directly provides cell-type ratios for all major GABAergic interneuron types in mouse LA and BA including NPY-containing neurogliaform cells (14-15%) and SST+ dendrite-targeting cells (10-16%), highly relevant to bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell and bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron.
summary: This study provides the first stereological estimates for total numbers and ratios of all major GABAergic neuron types in mouse LA and BA. Key findings: NPY-containing neurogliaform cells constitute 14-15% of GABAergic cells, axo-axonic cells 5.5-6%, PV+ basket cells 17-20%, CCK+ basket cells 7-9%, SST+ dendrite-targeting cells 10-16%, VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective cells 29-38%, and GABAergic projection neurons expressing SST and nNOS 5.5-8%.
quotes: NPY-containing neurogliaform cells (14%-15%), VIP and/or calretinin-expressing interneuron-selective interneurons (29%-38%), and GABAergic projection neurons expressing somatostatin and neuronal nitric oxide synthase (5.5%-8%).
The ratio of GABAergic neurons in the BA (22%) is significantly higher than in the LA (16%) in both male and female mice.

source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
section: PV+ interneurons targeting the perisomatic region of the principal cells
node_relevance_reason: Describes PV+/CB+ basket cells vs PV+/CB- axo-axonic cells in amygdala; moderately relevant to bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron by establishing that many PV+ basket cells co-express CB, but the node of interest is CB+/PV- dendrite-targeting, a distinct population.
summary: PV+ basket cells co-expressing calbindin (CB) innervate soma and proximal dendrites of principal neurons, while PV+ axo-axonic cells lack CB and target axon initial segments. PV+/CB+ basket cells constitute ~2.2% and ~4.7% of all neurons in LA and BA respectively. This distinction is important for differentiating CB+/PV- dendrite-targeting interneurons from CB+/PV+ basket cells.
quotes: PV+ basket cells expressing calbindin (CB) innervate the soma and the proximal dendrites of principal neurons, whereas PV+ axo-axonic cells lacking CB form synaptic contacts on axon initial segments.
PV+/CB+ basket cells constitute ~ 2.2 % and ~ 4.7 % of all neurons in LA and BA, respectively.

source_title: Transcriptomic diversity of amygdalar subdivisions across humans and nonhuman primates
node_relevance_reason: Provides cross-species (human, macaque, baboon) transcriptomic atlas of five amygdala nuclear subdivisions with both excitatory and inhibitory neuron subtypes, enabling human/NHP comparisons for all classical amygdala cell types under investigation.
summary: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of five amygdala nuclear subdivisions in macaques, baboons, and humans identified diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic neuron subtypes, highly conserved across primates. Compositional analyses revealed distinct classes of glutamatergic neurons and divergent parvalbumin and somatostatin GABAergic neuron expression profiles per BLC subdivision. Primate-specific specializations were identified for glutamatergic neurons by reference to murine amygdala atlases.
quotes: Compositional analyses revealed that subdivisions of the primate basolateral complex contain distinct classes of glutamatergic neurons and divergent gene expression profiles for parvalbumin and somatostatin GABAergic neurons.

Referencing primate neuron types to transcriptomic atlases of the murine amygdala highlighted primate-specific specializations for glutamatergic neurons and identified which neuron types are conserved across mammals and amygdalar subdivisions.

source_title: Facilitation of Contextual Fear Extinction by Orexin-1 Receptor Antagonism Is Associated with the Activation of Specific Amygdala Cell Subpopulations
node_relevance_reason: Directly identifies calbindin+ (but not parvalbumin+) GABAergic interneurons in BLA as specifically activated during contextual fear extinction consolidation, providing direct evidence for bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron and its functional role in fear extinction.
summary: Retrograde tracing combined with immunofluorescence showed that orexin-1 receptor antagonism (SB334867) increases activity of BLA neurons projecting to infralimbic mPFC during fear extinction. Specifically, GABAergic interneurons expressing calbindin — but not parvalbumin — were activated by orexin-1 receptor antagonism in BLA, identifying calbindin+ interneurons as a functional circuit element in fear extinction consolidation.
quotes: GABAergic interneurons expressing calbindin, but not parvalbumin, were also activated by orexin-1 receptor antagonism in the basolateral amygdala.
Treatment with the orexin-1 receptor antagonist SB334867 increased the activity of basolateral amygdala neurons projecting to infralimbic medial prefrontal cortex during fear extinction.

source_title: Immature excitatory neurons in the amygdala come of age during puberty
node_relevance_reason: Directly relevant to paralaminar_immature_neuron: describes the paralaminar nucleus (PL) population of immature excitatory neurons present at birth that mature through childhood and adolescence, including structural changes and relationship to sex hormones.
summary: The amygdala paralaminar nucleus (PL) contains a large population of immature excitatory neurons at birth, some of which may be born from local progenitors. Progenitors disappear in infancy but immature neurons persist throughout childhood and adolescence, maturing on a protracted timeline. PL maturation occurs predominantly during late childhood and puberty when sex hormone levels change.
quotes: The PL contains a large population of immature excitatory neurons at birth, some of which may continue to be born from local progenitors.
These progenitors disappear rapidly in infancy, but the immature neurons persist throughout childhood and adolescent ages, indicating that they develop on a protracted timeline.
PL maturation occurs predominately during late childhood and into puberty when sex hormone levels change.

source_title: Immature excitatory neurons in the amygdala come of age during puberty
section: Late-maturing neurons and other cell types in the PL
node_relevance_reason: Direct molecular evidence for paralaminar_immature_neuron: scRNA-seq identifies immature neuron cluster expressing DCX, BCL-2, MAP2, ROBO1, BCL11B, SOX11; majority are excitatory (TBR1+/VGLUT2+), confirming DCX as a key marker.
summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of human amygdala (ages 4-15) identified an immature neuron cluster differentially expressing DCX, BCL-2, MAP2, ROBO1, BCL11B, and SOX11. At age 13, 54.4% of DCX+ cells express TBR1 (excitatory neuron transcription factor) and 97.6% of mature TBR1+/NEUN+ neurons express VGLUT2. Only ~3% of PL cells express the GABAergic marker GAD67, confirming the majority of late-maturing PL neurons are excitatory.
quotes: Single cell RNA-sequencing of human amygdala samples from 4-15 years of age identified a cluster of immature neurons that differentially express many of the genes (e.g. DCX, BCL-2, MAP2) that were also identified by immunostaining, as well as novel genes (e.g. ROBO1, BCL11B, SOX11) that are related to ongoing neural developmental processes.
At 13 years of age, 54.4% of immature DCX + cells express T-box brain 1 (TBR1), an excitatory neuron transcription factor important for cortical excitatory neuron development.

Only about 3% of all cells in the PL express the GABAergic marker GAD67, and the number of cells in the PL expressing GAD67 or other interneuron markers such as SST, nNOS, or CR does not change with age.

source_title: Molecular characterization of Thy1 expressing fear-inhibiting neurons within the basolateral amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Directly relevant to basal_amygdala_extinction_neuron: Thy1-expressing neurons in BLA are functionally characterized as fear-inhibiting (extinction) neurons; silencing Thy1 neurons enhances fear expression and impairs extinction consolidation.
summary: Selective optical inhibition of Thy1-expressing BLA neurons during CS presentation enhanced within-session fear expression and blunted fear extinction consolidation, confirming that Thy1+ neurons are the fear-inhibiting (extinction) population in BLA. Genome-wide RNA sequencing was performed on isolated Thy1-eYFP+ neurons to characterize their molecular identity across the anterior-posterior axis of the amygdala.
quotes: Selective inhibition of Thy1 neurons appears to allow maintenance of activity of the previously silenced Fear-On circuitry.
The use of cell-type specific whole genome expression analysis allows in-depth interrogation of the molecular identity of a neural population of interest.

This approach has the advantage that the RNA sequencing data represents the average RNA content of Thy1-eYFP cells across the anterior-posterior axis of the amygdala as 8000-12,000 cells are isolated for each sample.

source_title: Developmental origin of the neuronal subtypes that comprise the amygdalar fear circuit in the mouse
node_relevance_reason: Relevant to developmental origins of basal amygdala fear circuit neurons: LA/BLA glutamatergic neurons derive from ventral pallium, CA (central amygdala) from vLGE, contextualizing the striatal-like nature of central amygdala and developmental origins relevant to cea_large/small_aspiny_neuron.
summary: Fate-mapping study establishes that LA/BLA projection neurons derive from ventral pallium (VP) progenitors, while central amygdala (CA) derives from vLGE progenitors, confirming its striatal character. Intercalated cells (ITCs) arise from dLGE and migrate laterally. Gsx2 and Sp8 conditional mutants confirm dLGE origin of ITCs.
quotes: progenitors in the ventral pallium (VP) contribute projection neurons to the LA and BLA but not the CA. Rather, the CA appears to derive, at least in part, from progenitors located in the ventral lateral ganglionic eminence (vLGE).

the ITCs arise from the dorsal lateral ganglionic eminence (dLGE) and migrate in the lateral migratory stream to populate the paracapsular regions as well as the main intercalated mass of the amygdala

source_title: Developmental origin of the neuronal subtypes that comprise the amygdalar fear circuit in the mouse
node_relevance_reason: Contextualizes the cellular composition of LA/BLA (glutamatergic projection neurons plus GABAergic interneurons) and CA (striatum-like GABAergic projection neurons), directly supporting node descriptions for basal_amygdala_fear_neuron and cea_large/small_aspiny_neuron.
summary: LA and BLA exhibit cortex-like characteristics with a majority of glutamatergic projection neurons, while the central amygdala (CA) contains striatum-like GABAergic projection neurons as its major output. Neuronal activity in all nuclei is modulated by diverse sets of inhibitory interneurons including intercalated cells (ITCs) clustered in paracapsular regions.
quotes: The LA and BLA represent the input to the amygdala and exhibit cortex-like characteristics with a majority of glutamatergic projection neurons.
Conversely, the CA contains striatum-like GABAergic projection neurons and represents the major output of the amygdala.

source_title: New Insights into the Pivotal Role of the Amygdala in Inflammation-Related Depression and Anxiety Disorder
section: The Basic Anatomy of the Amygdala: Structure and Connectivity
node_relevance_reason: Directly describes the striatum-like nature of CeA (GABAergic inhibitory neurons) and cortical-like BLA (80% glutamatergic, 20% GABAergic), supporting cea_large_aspiny_neuron and cea_small_aspiny_neuron node definitions.
summary: Provides clear cellular composition of BLA (cortical-like: 80% glutamatergic principal neurons, ~20% GABAergic inhibitory neurons) and CeA (striatum-like: primarily GABAergic inhibitory neurons). CeA is organized into CeL and CeM nuclei. BLA encodes threat value of stimuli; CeA coordinates behavioral output.
quotes: Developmentally, the BLA is a cortical-like structure consisting of 80% glutamatergic principal neurons and approximately 20% GABAergic inhibitory neurons.
In contrast, CeA is a striatum-like structure that primarily comprises GABAergic inhibitory neurons.
the BLA is widely known to encode the threat value of a stimulus, while the CeA is responsible for coordinating the behavioral output.

source_title: Rho GTPases in the Amygdala—A Switch for Fears?
section: The Amygdala Is the Fear Center in the Brain
node_relevance_reason: Provides broad anatomical overview of amygdala with cell-type background (spiny glutamatergic BLA neurons, GABAergic CEA neurons); background context only, no specific molecular markers for target nodes.
summary: This review describes the anatomical organization of BLA (BA, BM, LA) and CEA (CEl, CEm) with GABAergic processing. The majority of BLA neurons are spiny glutamatergic (with minority GABAergic interneurons), while CEl and CEm mainly contain GABAergic neurons. The ICMs consist of dopamine type-1 and mu-opioid-receptor expressing cells.
quotes: The majority of BLA neurons are spiny glutamatergic neurons (with a minority of GABAergic interneurons).
CEl and CEm mainly contain GABAergic neurons.

source_title: Persistent pain intensifies recall of consolidated fear memories
node_relevance_reason: Provides evidence for calbindin+ and parvalbumin+ interneuron populations in BLA with functional significance for fear memory; relevant to bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron (Calb-ir neurons described as targeting dendrites of pyramidal cells) and contextualizes BLA-to-mPFC projections as fear/extinction neurons.
summary: Neuropathic pain increased the number of PV+ interneurons in BLA but not total calbindin+ neurons; increased PV/CB double-positive cells suggest pain-induced phenotypic change in CB interneurons. BLA projection neurons connecting to mPFC (fear/extinction neurons) receive increased inhibitory input from PV+ interneurons under chronic pain. CB interneurons in BLA are described as targeting dendrites of pyramidal cells and synchronizing activity to hypothalamic inputs.
quotes: Despite being fewer in number than excitatory neurons, inhibitory interneurons in the BLA are essential for acquisition of fear memories.
the Calb interneurons target the dendrites of the pyramidal cells and synchronize their activity to hypothalamic inputs
the BLA projection neurons can be categorized as 'fear neurons' and 'extinction neurons' according to their activity in response to the conditioning stimulus

source_title: The role of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-kinase A in regulating emotional behavior and amygdala function
node_relevance_reason: Describes IP3K-A expression in CeA (GABAergic interneurons) and BLA (CAMKIIα+ excitatory neurons) with functional effects on fear/anxiety behavior; no specific cell-type morphological characterization for target nodes.
summary: IP3K-A protein is highly enriched in CeA (colocalizing with GAD67+ GABAergic neurons) and BLA (colocalizing with CAMKIIα+ excitatory pyramidal neurons). KO mice show reduced c-Fos in BLA and CeA, altered fear/anxiety behavior, and genome-wide gene expression changes including in fear-, anxiety-, and PTSD-related genes.
quotes: In the CeA, IP3K-A primarily colocalized with GAD67-positive GABAergic interneurons, whereas most IP3K-A in the BLA was in CAMKIIα-positive excitatory pyramidal neurons.
IP3K-A expression is highly enriched in the amygdala; immunoreactivity is particularly strong in the CeA and BLA.

source_title: Neuronal physiology of amygdala neurons in the context of injury and pain
node_relevance_reason: Review directly enumerates known amygdala cell types and their electrophysiology (LA-BLA pyramidal neurons, four interneuron classes including CB+ dendrite-targeting, SST+ neurons in CeL); relevant to bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron, cea_large/small_aspiny_neuron, and BLA fear circuit neurons.
summary: This electrophysiology review of amygdala neurons describes LA-BLA interneuron subtypes (axo-axonic, CB+ dendrite-targeting, AStria, PV+) based on in-vivo recordings. For CeA, SST+ and CRF+ neurons are characterized with early-spiking and late-firing phenotypes. References Vereczki et al. (2021) for complete LA-BA interneuron ratios including NPY+ neurogliaform cells (14-15%) and SST+ dendrite-targeting cells (10-16%).
quotes: Bienvenu et al. (2012) categorized rat LA-BLA interneuron subtypes from in to vivo electrophysiological recordings based on their connectivity patterns, spontaneous firing frequencies, and responses to noxious mechanical stimuli in naïve animals. This categorization resulted in four classes of LA-BLA interneurons: axo-axonic, CB+ (calbindin-positive) dendrite-targeting, AStria (amygdalo-striatal transition area), and PV+ (parvalbumin-positive).
NPY-containing neurogliaform cells are 14-15 %, VIP and/or calretinin (CR)-expressing interneuron-selective interneurons are the most abundant at 29-38 %
